Root.actionsRef.type: RefObject<{ unmount: () => void; close: () => void } | null>

NO modal.semantic: props = Omit<DialogRoot.Props, 'modal'|'disablePointerDismissal'|'onOpenChange'|'actionsRef'|'handle'> — AlertDialog is ALWAYS modal and outside-press dismissal cannot be disabled

dataAttributes: Backdrop / Popup / Viewport / Close: identical to Dialog — data-open, data-closed, data-starting-style, data-ending-style, data-nested, data-nested-dialog-open (Popup+Viewport), data-disabled (Close), CSS var --nested-dialogs
Backdrop/Popup/Viewport/Close/Description/Title are literally the Dialog parts re-exported from ../dialog/*
renderProp: Same per-part `render` prop as Dialog (ReactElement | (props, state) => ReactElement) via useRender.
controlled: Identical to Dialog: defaultOpen/open + triggerId/defaultTriggerId, onOpenChange(open, eventDetails), actionsRef, AlertDialog.createHandle() handle (open/openWithPayload/close/isOpen).
formIntegration: None — no hidden inputs, no name/value or validation wiring. Close renders a native <button>.
keyboard: Always modal: focus is trapped, page scroll locked, outside pointer interactions disabled, and Escape closes (topmost only). No arrow-key navigation. Focus restore through Popup finalFocus.
notableDifferences: AlertDialog is always modal — `modal` and `disablePointerDismissal` are explicitly omitted from its props type, so an alert dialog can never be made dismissable-by-outside-press. React Aria's AlertDialog is likewise non-dismissable but expresses it differently.

Most parts are the Dialog parts themselves (Backdrop/Close/Description/Popup/Portal/Title/Viewport are re-exported from ../dialog/*) — style classes written for Dialog apply verbatim to AlertDialog, and only the Root (alertdialog semantics) and Trigger differ.
Naming: open/defaultOpen/onOpenChange instead of isOpen/onOpenChange(isOpen); role='alertdialog' is built in rather than passed.
Same data-starting-style/data-ending-style animation contract as Dialog; no render-prop style functions.
